description: Illustrative instance showing BOTH shapes the ledger carries: a merge that received its declared two-person quorum, and a merge that did not. The approved row is what a governed landing looks like — two DISTINCT approving principals and a sealed evidence pack id. The breach row cannot claim approval: retro_approved is pinned false by the schema, so an irreversible action performed without its approver can only be recorded, never retro-blessed.

enforcement_boundary.reason: Illustrative boundary. Commits landing before the enforcement point existed are honestly out of scope rather than silently excluded.

breaches.note: Illustrative breach row. A landing recorded here is a permanent admission, not a variance and not a waiver: the gate stops failing on it because it is DECLARED, never because it was excused.
